ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Let the equal time interval before and after the acceleration reversal be T, and take the initial acceleration direction as positive. The object starts from rest, so after the first interval its velocity is v_m = a_1 T, and its displacement is s_1 = (1/2)a_1 T^2. During the second equal interval, the acceleration reverses direction and has magnitude a_2, so the acceleration is -a_2. The additional displacement is s_2 = v_m T - (1/2)a_2 T^2 = a_1 T^2 - (1/2)a_2 T^2. Since the object returns to its starting point, the total displacement is zero: (1/2)a_1 T^2 + a_1 T^2 - (1/2)a_2 T^2 = 0. Thus (3/2)a_1 T^2 = (1/2)a_2 T^2, giving a_2 = 3a_1, so a_1/a_2 = 1/3. The final velocity is v_f = a_1T - a_2T = a_1T - 3a_1T = -2a_1T. Its speed is 5 m/s, so 2a_1T = 5, hence a_1T = 2.5 m/s. Therefore the velocity magnitude when the acceleration changes is v_m = 2.5 m/s, and a_1/a_2 = 1/3.

During the second interval, acceleration is in the opposite direction, so the velocity line slopes downward and ends at -5 m/s, because the object must return to the start and the final speed is 5 m/s in the opposite direction.
